topic.title: Translating umbilical cord blood extracellular vesicles into a novel therapy for postpartum alopecia: a mechanistic and preclinical review
topic.abstract: Postpartum alopecia (PPA) is a common physiological hair loss in women, characterized by complex pathogenesis involving abrupt postpartum hormonal withdrawal, disrupted hair follicle cycling, local microenvironmental inflammation, and oxidative stress. Umbilical cord blood-derived extracellular vesicles (UCB-EVs)-nanosized, lipid-bilayer-enclosed particles enriched with microRNAs, growth factors, and proteins-have shown considerable promise in regenerative medicine owing to their low immunogenicity, high biocompatibility, and tissue-repair capacity. This review systematically summarizes the current state of research on UCB-EVs in the context of PPA, focusing on their proposed molecular mechanisms in hair follicle regeneration, hair-cycle modulation, antiinflammatory effects, and antioxidative stress responses. Importantly, the available evidence remains largely preclinical, derived from in vitro and animal-model studies; direct clinical evidence for UCBEVs in PPA is still lacking. UCB-EVs should therefore be regarded as a promising investigational strategy, and their clinical translation will require rigorous validation of standardization, safety, and efficacy.

Epidemiological data indicates that the prevalence of PPA is remarkably high, with studies suggesting that over 90% of postpartum women experience some degree of hair loss (3).

At the molecular level, UCB-EVs are enriched with specific miRNAs, such as miR-21-5p and let-7b-5p, which are capable of targeting and modulating key signaling pathways critical for hair follicle biology (2).

sections.title: Biological characteristics and preparation of UCB-EVs
sentences: They are broadly classified into exosomes (30–150 nm), microvesicles (100–1000 nm), and apoptotic bodies (>1000 nm) based on their biogenesis and size (9).

This typically involves a combination of techniques: This typically involves a combination of techniques: dynamic light scattering (DLS), also known as photon correlation spectroscopy, which measures time-dependent fluctuations in scattered light caused by Brownian motion of particles to determine the hydrodynamic diameter and polydispersity index (PDI) of EVs (21); Nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) to determine particle size distribution and concentration (13, 14); Western blot analysis to confirm the presence of EV protein markers such as CD63, CD81, and TSG101 (13, 15); and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) or cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) to verify the characteristic spherical, lipid bilayer morphology of the vesicles (14, 22).

sections.title: Pathogenesis of postpartum hair loss in women and limitations of current treatments
sentences: In fact, the prevalence of thyroid abnormalities in patients with telogen effluvium has been documented to be between 5.7% and 17%, underscoring the importance of screening for postpartum thyroiditis in patients presenting with persistent postpartum hair loss (30).

Studies show that low ferritin is significantly associated with telogen effluvium, and vitamin D, which acts as a hormone, is crucial for proper hair follicle cycling through its involvement in signaling pathways of growth and differentiation (33–35).

Evidence from other forms of alopecia, such as that seen in COVID-19, suggests that severe systemic inflammation can dramatically increase the risk of telogen effluvium, with patients exhibiting higher levels of inflammatory biomarkers like C-reactive protein and IL-1β correlating with increased hair shedding (36).
These cytokines directly inhibit the proliferation of hair follicle stem cells and keratinocytes, by activating signaling cascades, most notably the JAK-STAT pathway (38–40).

sections.title: Preclinical evidence for UCB-EVs in treating postpartum hair loss
sentences: When DPCs, the master regulators of hair follicle cycling, were treated with UCB-EVs at a concentration of 50 μg/mL for 48 hours, significant cellular responses were observed, including a 45% increase in proliferation and a 35% reduction in apoptosis (55).

sections.label: 결론
sections.title: Clinical translation challenges and future directions of UCB-EVs for postpartum hair loss
sentences: A primary hurdle is the limited volume of UCB obtainable per unit, as a single cord blood donation yields only approximately 10^10 to 10^11 EV particles.

For instance, the use of a chemically defined, xeno- and blood-free culture medium, such as Oxium™EXO, has been shown to increase small EV (sEV) secretion from MSCs by three-fold, consistently across multiple harvest time points and different cell sources, yielding an enrichment of particles within the 51–200 nm range (71).

Preclinical safety evaluations using non-human primates have shown that high-dose intravenous administration of human UCB-MSC-derived exosomes (3.85 × 10^12 particles) did not cause significant adverse effects on general clinical conditions, hematology, coagulation, or immune organs, and did not induce major changes in immunoglobulins or cytokines (79).

sections.label: 결론
sections.title: Conclusion
sentences: Transcriptomic analyses have revealed the involvement of immune cells and ferroptosis in frontal fibrosing alopecia (81).

원문: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42857222/

[한눈에 보기]
- Postpartum alopecia (PPA) is a common physiological hair loss in women, characterized by complex pathogenesis involving abrupt postpartum hormonal withdrawal, disrupted hair follicle cycling, local microenvironmental inflammation, and oxidative stress.
- Umbilical cord blood-derived extracellular vesicles (UCB-EVs)-nanosized, lipid-bilayer-enclosed particles enriched with microRNAs, growth factors, and proteins-have shown considerable promise in regenerative medicine owing to their low immunogenicity, high biocompatibility, and tissue-repair capacity.
- This review systematically summarizes the current state of research on UCB-EVs in the context of PPA, focusing on their proposed molecular mechanisms in hair follicle regeneration, hair-cycle modulation, antiinflammatory effects, and antioxidative stress responses.

[상세 내용] (논문 전문 7개 섹션에서 발췌)

◆ 배경 — Introduction
  · Female postpartum alopecia (PPA) represents a significant clinical and psychosocial challenge, emerging as one of the most common dermatological conditions affecting women in the postpartum period.
  · Epidemiological data indicates that the prevalence of PPA is remarkably high, with studies suggesting that over 90% of postpartum women experience some degree of hair loss (3).
  · At the molecular level, UCB-EVs are enriched with specific miRNAs, such as miR-21-5p and let-7b-5p, which are capable of targeting and modulating key signaling pathways critical for hair follicle biology (2).

◆ 그 밖의 내용 — Biological characteristics and preparation of UCB-EVs
  · They are broadly classified into exosomes (30–150 nm), microvesicles (100–1000 nm), and apoptotic bodies (>1000 nm) based on their biogenesis and size (9).
  · This typically involves a combination of techniques: This typically involves a combination of techniques: dynamic light scattering (DLS), also known as photon correlation spectroscopy, which measures time-dependent fluctuations in scattered light caused by Brownian motion of particles to determine the hydrodynamic diameter and polydispersity index (PDI) of EVs (21); Nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) to determine particle size distribution and concentration (13, 14); Western blot analysis to confirm the presence of EV protein markers such as CD63, CD81, and TSG101 (13, 15); and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) or cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) to verify the characteristic spherical, lipid bilayer morphology of the vesicles (14, 22).

◆ 고찰 — Pathogenesis of postpartum hair loss in women and limitations of current treatments
  · In fact, the prevalence of thyroid abnormalities in patients with telogen effluvium has been documented to be between 5.7% and 17%, underscoring the importance of screening for postpartum thyroiditis in patients presenting with persistent postpartum hair loss (30).
  · Studies show that low ferritin is significantly associated with telogen effluvium, and vitamin D, which acts as a hormone, is crucial for proper hair follicle cycling through its involvement in signaling pathways of growth and differentiation (33–35).
  · Evidence from other forms of alopecia, such as that seen in COVID-19, suggests that severe systemic inflammation can dramatically increase the risk of telogen effluvium, with patients exhibiting higher levels of inflammatory biomarkers like C-reactive protein and IL-1β correlating with increased hair shedding (36).
  · These cytokines directly inhibit the proliferation of hair follicle stem cells and keratinocytes, by activating signaling cascades, most notably the JAK-STAT pathway (38–40).

◆ 그 밖의 내용 — Molecular mechanisms of UCB-EVs in promoting hair follicle regeneration

◆ 그 밖의 내용 — Preclinical evidence for UCB-EVs in treating postpartum hair loss
  · When DPCs, the master regulators of hair follicle cycling, were treated with UCB-EVs at a concentration of 50 μg/mL for 48 hours, significant cellular responses were observed, including a 45% increase in proliferation and a 35% reduction in apoptosis (55).

◆ 결론 — Clinical translation challenges and future directions of UCB-EVs for postpartum hair loss
  · A primary hurdle is the limited volume of UCB obtainable per unit, as a single cord blood donation yields only approximately 10^10 to 10^11 EV particles.
  · For instance, the use of a chemically defined, xeno- and blood-free culture medium, such as Oxium™EXO, has been shown to increase small EV (sEV) secretion from MSCs by three-fold, consistently across multiple harvest time points and different cell sources, yielding an enrichment of particles within the 51–200 nm range (71).

  · Transcriptomic analyses have revealed the involvement of immune cells and ferroptosis in frontal fibrosing alopecia (81).
